title: Mixed Abstraction Level Routine
pattern: A single function mixes high-level coordination calls (e.g., dispatch events, log phases) directly with low-level details (e.g., raw byte manipulation, string splitting, or mathematical formulas).
why_bad: It violates the Composed Method pattern. Combining levels of detail makes it incredibly difficult for a reader to understand the function's core intent, as the high-level policy is obscured by noise.
detection: A function contains both calls to high-level domain methods and raw low-level operations (loops, string cleaners, raw regexes).
counterexample: Extremely small functions (less than 10 lines) where low-level implementation is the entire purpose of the routine.
source: *Robert C. Martin - Clean Code, Chapter 3 (Functions), Section "One Level of Abstraction per Function"*
